Synopsis:
    A fuel oil supply deficit of ~218,000 bpd is forecast for Q3 2026, driven by war-related refinery damage in Russia and the Middle East, reduced Chinese refining exports, and Houthi-driven shipping diversions. Refiners globally are prioritising diesel, gasoline and jet fuel over fuel oil to capture higher margins, compounding the shortage. Stocks in key hubs (Singapore, ARA, Fujairah) sit ~30% below seasonal 3-year averages. Very low sulphur fuel oil (VLSFO) prices are up 76% since the Iran war began. Russia's fuel oil exports hit a record low in August; Kuwait's Al-Zour refinery is near-idle. The crunch is most acute in Asia but has global ripple effects through shipping costs and power generation economics.

Q01. Is the content's main message about EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
Relevance: NO — The article is primarily about global fuel oil (bunker/power plant fuel) supply disruption. The ARA hub is mentioned peripherally as a storage reference point, but there is no direct focus on EU energy policy, German power prices or German energy economics.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 62 — The geopolitical disruption backdrop (Ukraine drone strikes on Russian refineries, Houthi threats, Iran war) is broadly known. However, the magnitude of the deficit (218,000 bpd in Q3), the record-low Russian fuel oil exports, and Al-Zour's near-complete outage add material new data points that go beyond consensus expectations, lifting the score into moderately-to-high uncertainty territory.

Q03. Is the content explicit about bullish impact on the German power futures market?
Explicit: NO
Impact score: 12 — There is no direct reference to German power futures. An indirect, weak bullish channel exists: fuel oil is used in power generation, tighter fuel oil supply and higher costs could marginally support gas and coal demand as substitutes, feeding into European power price dynamics. The link is tenuous and not explicit in the article.
